installExtension.step3: Open the popup and start from the campus shortcuts you use most often.

whatIsLinku.question: What is LinKU?
whatIsLinku.answer: LinKU is a Chrome-extension-first companion for Konkuk University workflows, paired with a public SEO site and authenticated web routes on the same canonical domain.

withoutExtension.question: Can I use LinKU without installing the extension?
withoutExtension.answer: Yes for guides, install help, feature overviews, FAQs, and service landing pages. The fastest campus workflows still live in the Chrome extension.

authenticatedSurface.question: What is the authenticated web surface for?
authenticatedSurface.answer: It handles Google sign-in, personal favorites, settings, account management, and extension connection status inside path-based routes such as /login and /dashboard.

supportedBrowser.question: Which browser is supported first?
supportedBrowser.answer: This MVP is designed around Chrome and Chrome Web Store distribution because the core flows depend on browser extension capabilities.

domainPolicy.question: How are the domains organized now?
domainPolicy.answer: The public pages and authenticated routes both live on the single canonical domain https://www.linku.xxx, while the apex domain redirects there and api.linku.xxx remains optional for a future BFF split.

monorepoFoundation.title: Monorepo foundation
monorepoFoundation.summary: The workspace now separates the extension, shared packages, and the upcoming single-domain web surface.
monorepoFoundation.bullet1: The existing Chrome extension lives in apps/extension.
monorepoFoundation.bullet2: Shared UI, config, platform, SEO, and type packages are now part of the workspace.
monorepoFoundation.bullet3: Public web content and authenticated route helpers are being prepared around a single canonical domain.

singleDomainWeb.title: Single-domain web direction
singleDomainWeb.summary: The split between www and app subdomains was removed in favor of one Next.js app on the canonical web domain.
singleDomainWeb.bullet1: Public SEO routes and authenticated routes will both run on www.linku.xxx.
singleDomainWeb.bullet2: Canonical URLs, OAuth callbacks, and session handling now share the same base URL.
singleDomainWeb.bullet3: Authenticated routes follow a noindex policy by default.

site.footerBlurb: LinKU runs public SEO pages and authenticated entry routes on the same canonical web domain.

app.summary: Signed in on the same canonical domain used by the public SEO surface.

meta.title: Privacy
meta.description: Read the privacy baseline for LinKU public pages, authenticated routes, and extension-adjacent account flows.

privacy.headline: A practical privacy baseline for a single-domain LinKU deployment.
privacy.body: Public pages, authenticated routes, and extension-adjacent flows have different data needs even when they live on the same canonical domain.
privacy.point1: Public pages should stay readable without requiring sign-in or client-only rendering.
privacy.point2: Authenticated routes should use server-verifiable sessions, minimal secrets exposure, and noindex rules.
privacy.point3: Extension-specific tokens and privileged browser APIs remain in the Chrome extension instead of the public web surface.

meta.title: Login
meta.description: Enter the authenticated LinKU surface on the same canonical domain used for public SEO pages and install guidance.

login.headline: Sign in without leaving the canonical LinKU domain.
login.body: Public discovery pages, install guidance, and account routes now live together. Google OAuth lands here first, then carries the session forward to /dashboard, /favorites, /settings, and /extension/connect.
login.cardBody: Auth.js handles the same-domain session shell here. If Google credentials are not configured yet, the route still renders and stays noindex so the rest of the app can be validated safely.
login.configure: Configure Google OAuth to enable sign-in

favorites.headline: Keep the routes you never want to re-find.
favorites.body: This MVP stores favorites in a replaceable cookie-backed workspace layer so the interface is ready for a future database-backed implementation.
